cards.text: Paul the apostle is on his way to Jerusalem, and he just told the elders of the church in Ephesus they'd never see his face again, and they all wept (Acts 20:22, 25, 37-38). In town after town, the Holy Spirit has warned him that chains and afflictions are waiting (Acts 20:23). Now Paul and his travel crew tear themselves away and sail to Cos, then Rhodes, then Patara.

cards.question: At Patara, Paul's crew finds a ship crossing over to a new region. Where's it headed?

cards.text: They spot Cyprus, pass south of it and land at Tyre in Syria. And friend, that ship isn't stopping because Paul asked nicely.

cards.question: So why does the ship stop at Tyre?

cards.text: They look up the disciples in Tyre and stay SEVEN DAYS. That's not a layover, friend, that's moving in.

cards.question: Through the Spirit, the disciples in Tyre keep telling Paul not to go up to ___.
After all those warnings in Tyre, Paul calls off the trip and stays there.

cards.text: When the week's up, the whole church walks them out of the city, wives and children too. That's not a goodbye, friend. That's a PARADE.

cards.question: Down on the beach outside Tyre, what does everyone do before Paul's crew leaves?

answers.text: Read a letter from Ephesus together

cards.question: After the farewells on the beach, the disciples from Tyre board the ship and sail on with Paul's crew.

cards.text: The voyage from Tyre ends at Ptolemais, where Paul's crew greets the brothers and stays with them for a day.

Leaving the next day, they go on to Caesarea and stay at the home of Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven chosen to serve the church back in Acts 6:5. Tyre got a week and Ptolemais got a day, but I stayed in a junk drawer for YEARS without a single invitation.

cards.question: Philip has four unmarried daughters who prophesy.

cards.text: Several days in, a prophet named Agabus comes down from Judea. Watch this one, friend.
Agabus walks over, takes a belt and ties up his own feet and hands with it. No hello, no small talk, friend, just a grown man tying himself up in the middle of the visit.

cards.question: Agabus ties up his own hands and feet with a belt. Whose belt is it?
Agabus says the Holy Spirit says the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the ___.

cards.text: Paul's crew and the people of Caesarea hear it, and they ALL plead with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem. Me? I'd have wrapped my mustache around his ankle and held on.

cards.question: Paul answers the people pleading with him. For the name of the Lord Jesus, what does he say he's ready for in Jerusalem?

answers.text: To be bound and even to die
To argue his case in court
To preach and then slip away

cards.question: Paul tells the people pleading with him that their weeping is breaking his heart.
Paul won't be talked out of going, so his friends quiet down. What do they say?

answers.text: May the Lord go with you
May the Lord keep you safe

cards.text: After these days, they pack up and go on to Jerusalem, warnings and all. One rain alert on my phone and I cancel EVERYTHING, friend.

cards.question: Who goes along with Paul's crew on the way to Jerusalem?

cards.text: Those disciples take them to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple. Friend, this man has a guest room waiting in every town.

findings.problem: Card 1 has already explicitly said that Paul is on his way to Jerusalem, giving away "Jerusalem" as the answer to this card's blank before the question is asked.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Card 2 gives no basis for knowing the unseen statement about Philip's daughters, card 5 gives no basis for identifying the belt's owner, card 6 asks for an unseen word in Agabus's prophecy with no basis for choosing among the three peoples, and card 10 offers three plausible responses without establishing what the friends conclude. These make four of the stop's seven choice cards discovery guesses, so most of its choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The nearest antecedent to "this man" is Mnason, so the joke sounds as though Mnason has guest rooms waiting in every town. If it is meant to describe Paul continually finding hosts, the unclear referent keeps the joke from clicking without explanation.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
